source_text: Nobis etsi quaerendum est adhuc et semper, ubi tamen quaeri oportet? Apud haereticos, ubi omnia extranea et adversaria nostrae veritati, ad quos vetamur accedere? Quis servus cibaria ab extraneo, ne dicam ab inimico domini sui, sperat? Quis miles ab infoederatis, ne dicam ab hostibus regibus, donativum et stipendium captat, nisi plane desertor et transfuga et rebellis? Etiam anus illa intra tectum suum drachmam requirebat, etiam pulsator ille vicini ianuam tundebat, etiam vidua illa non inimicum, licet durum, iudicem interpellabat. Nemo inde instrui potest unde destruitur; nemo ab eo inluminatur a quo contenebratur. Quaeramus ergo in nostro et a nostris et de nostro, idque dumtaxat quod salva regula fidei potest in quaestionem devenire.
orientation: Tertullian has just shown that the command to seek was for those who had not yet found; now he asks where any remaining seeking may rightly be done.
pass_a_gloss: For us, even if seeking is still to be done and always, where nevertheless ought it to be sought? Among heretics, where all things are foreign and hostile to our truth, to whom we are forbidden to approach? What slave hopes for food from a stranger, not to say from an enemy of his master? What soldier seeks a gift and pay from those not bound by treaty, not to say from enemy kings, unless plainly a deserter and a turncoat and a rebel? Even that old woman was searching for the drachma within her own house, even that knocker was beating on the door of a neighbor, even that widow was appealing to a judge who was not an enemy, though he was harsh. No one can be instructed from that by which he is destroyed; no one is enlightened by that by which he is darkened. Let us seek therefore in our own and from our own and about our own, and that only which, with the rule of faith safe, can come into question.

choices.why: Keeps the legal and military flavor of the Latin: extranea means outside one's own household or camp, adversaria means actively opposed.
Renders the precise Roman military term for peoples outside a treaty relationship, preserving the soldier metaphor.
Captat has a grasping, opportunistic force, fitting the soldier who improperly tries to get pay from the wrong source.

choices.english: with the rule of faith safe
choices.why: Uses the required glossary term 'rule of faith' and renders the ablative absolute literally, preserving the condition that the rule remains unharmed.
rejected: without harming the rule of faith
provided the rule of faith is preserved

choices.why: Devenire suggests arriving at a point; the phrase marks the limit of legitimate inquiry.

pass_b_english: Even if we must still seek, and always seek, where should the seeking happen? Among heretics, where everything is foreign and hostile to our truth, and where we are forbidden to go? What servant hopes to get food from a stranger—not to say from his own master's enemy? What soldier seeks a gift and pay from those not bound by treaty—not to say from enemy kings—unless he is plainly a deserter, a turncoat, and a rebel? Even that old woman was searching for her drachma inside her own house; even that man was knocking at his neighbor's door; even that widow was pleading with a judge who was not her enemy, though he was harsh. No one can be built up from the place where he is destroyed; no one is enlightened by the one who darkens him. So let us seek in our own, from our own, and about our own—and only what can come into question with the rule of faith safe.
